tasks.short: Work out costs for purchases and customer quotes from supplier quotes, price lists and overhead rates.

today.trigger: A department asks for a cost estimate, a supplier quote arrives, or sales needs a cost price for a warehousing tender.
steps: Collect supplier quotes and price lists from Outlook and SharePoint
Copy line items and prices into an Excel costing sheet
Add overhead rates, fuel surcharges and labour cost from AFAS figures
Check totals against earlier comparable calculations
Send the result to the requester or the controller
drudgery: Retyping quote lines from PDFs
Looking up the current overhead and labour rates
Rebuilding the same sheet for every request
today.time_sinks: Retyping PDF quotes and finding the right current rates take most of the time; the actual calculation is quick.

lenses.faster: Quote PDFs are read into structured lines automatically and a fixed costing template applies the current rates, so retyping and rate hunting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: When a quote lands in the purchasing mailbox, the extraction and a draft cost sheet are ready before the bookkeeper opens it.
lenses.ambitious: Every warehousing and transport tender gets a full cost price per site, including flex labour and fuel, instead of a rough estimate on the big ones only.
lenses.joy: No more copying numbers from scanned PDFs; the bookkeeper spends time on the odd lines and on questioning a price that looks wrong.
lenses.options: Produce three versions per request: cheapest supplier, preferred supplier and a scenario with higher fuel or CAO wage increases.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the costing template and the rate table, and checks the extraction quality instead of filling in sheets.
reach: FP&A Analyst: cost assumptions for forecasts
Controller: cost price checks for tenders

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier quotes are really comparable, which overhead rate applies to which site, and when a price looks too good to be true.
tasks.pattern_why: Quotes arrive as unstructured PDFs and emails; a model turns them into structured lines, and the costing itself is fixed arithmetic in a template.

in_practice.trigger: Quote or price list arrives in the shared purchasing mailbox, or a costing request is logged.
steps: Model extracts supplier, items, quantities, unit prices and terms from the PDF
Template applies current overhead, labour and fuel rates kept in one rate table
Script flags lines with low extraction confidence or prices far from earlier quotes
Bookkeeper reviews flags and approves the cost sheet
Approved sheet is saved to SharePoint and sent to the requester
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every cost sheet before it is sent; the controller approves tender cost prices.
systems: Azure OpenAI or similar model service
data_needed: Overhead and labour rates per site
Historical quotes per item and supplier
in_practice.logs_to: Costing register in SharePoint with source file, extracted lines, rates used and approver.

evidence.claim: Language models can extract line items from supplier quote PDFs into structured tables.
Microsoft Copilot in Excel can help build and explain formulas in costing sheets.

risks: Extraction errors on scanned or multi-page quotes going unnoticed
Rate table not kept current after CAO wage increases
Requesters treating a draft estimate as a firm price
research_questions: How many costing requests per month come in, and how many follow a repeatable template?
What share of supplier quotes are machine-readable PDFs versus scans or email text?
Is there one agreed overhead and labour rate per site that finance and sales both accept?

tasks.short: Match Rabobank statement lines to invoices and bookings in AFAS and clear the differences.

today.trigger: Daily bank statement import from Rabobank into AFAS, plus month end.
steps: Import the Rabobank statement file into AFAS Profit
Let AFAS auto-match payments with clear references
Manually search for invoices behind unmatched receipts and payments
Book bank costs, interest and unknown items to suspense accounts
Chase colleagues or customers about unclear items
drudgery: Searching for invoices when customers pay several at once without references
Booking recurring bank charges by hand
Clearing the suspense account at month end
today.time_sinks: Customer payments with missing or wrong references and combined payments for many invoices.

lenses.faster: Rules plus fuzzy matching on amount, name, date and partial references clear most of the lines that are manual today.
lenses.autonomous: Each morning the statement is imported, matched and booked; the bookkeeper only sees a short list of exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Daily reconciled cash and a suspense account at zero every day, so cash position and DSO are reliable at any time, not just at month end.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for which invoices a lump sum payment covers; the remaining work is resolving genuine disputes.
lenses.options: For an unmatched receipt, show the three most likely invoice combinations with a confidence score instead of one guess.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the matching rules and reviews the auto-match rate each week instead of matching lines.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: spotting short payments and disputes early

tasks.human_edge: Judging unclear payments, calling a customer about a short payment, and deciding where a strange item belongs.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank lines and open items are structured; matching rules can be written down and the result is checkable, with a small model step only for free-text references.

in_practice.trigger: New Rabobank statement file (CAMT.053) available each morning.
steps: Statement imported automatically into AFAS Profit
Matching rules and fuzzy match on amount, name and reference propose matches
High-confidence matches and recurring bank costs booked automatically
Exceptions listed with suggested invoice combinations
Bookkeeper resolves exceptions and contacts customers where needed
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves exceptions and any match below the confidence threshold; auto-booking rules are approved by the controller.
data_needed: Customer and supplier bank account numbers
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS booking history plus an exceptions log with who resolved each item and why.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports bank statements and automatically matches payments to open items.
Rabobank offers automatic statement export in CAMT.053 format for accounting software.

risks: Wrong auto-matches hiding a customer short payment
Rules drift as customers change payment habits
Over-reliance makes the team lose knowledge of odd cases
research_questions: What is the current AFAS auto-match rate, and which line types make up the manual remainder?
How many customers pay several invoices in one transfer without references?
What error rate on auto-matches would the controller and auditor accept?

tasks.short: Put together AP and AR reports: open items, ageing, cash in and out, P&L tables for finance.

today.trigger: Weekly AR/AP overview, month-end close pack, and ad hoc requests from the controller or Finance Director.
steps: Export open items and ledger data from AFAS to Excel
Clean and pivot the data into ageing and cash tables
Copy tables into the standard report template
Add short notes on large or old items
Email the report to controller and managers
drudgery: Same export and pivot every week
Fixing formatting and broken links in templates
Answering follow-up questions by making another export
today.time_sinks: Manual exports, cleaning and rebuilding the same tables each period.

lenses.faster: Standard reports come straight from the nightly AFAS extract in Power BI, so exports and pivots disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Ageing and cash reports refresh nightly and are sent on a schedule; a model drafts the notes on the largest movements for review.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets their own AR and AP view weekly, and finance can answer drill-down questions on the spot.
lenses.joy: The bookkeeper stops rebuilding spreadsheets and spends the time explaining what the numbers mean.
lenses.options: Offer the same data cut by site, customer group or agency, chosen by the reader in the dashboard.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper defines the report set and the data checks, and keeps the definitions consistent with the controller.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: collection priority lists
FP&A Analyst: actuals feeding the forecast

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which numbers will raise questions and writing the one line that explains them.
tasks.pattern_why: Data is structured in AFAS and reports have fixed definitions; dashboards and scheduled reports run without a model, with an optional model draft for commentary.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh; weekly and month-end schedule.
steps: Power BI refreshes AR, AP, cash and P&L tables from the AFAS extract
Data checks compare totals with the AFAS trial balance
Model drafts notes on the biggest changes and overdue items
Bookkeeper edits notes and releases the report
Scheduled email or Teams post to recipients
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper reviews and releases the commentary; tables publish automatically only if data checks pass.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history and a release log in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI scheduled refresh and subscriptions deliver reports automatically.
Copilot in Power BI can draft narrative summaries of report visuals.

risks: Nightly extract fails silently and stale numbers go out
Model-written notes state a wrong cause for a movement
Different report definitions between finance and site managers
research_questions: Which of today's Excel reports already have a Power BI equivalent that nobody uses?
Does the nightly AFAS extract contain open-item detail with due dates?
Do readers trust automated commentary, or do they want a named person behind each note?

tasks.short: Run the trial balance in AFAS at month end and check accounts before the controller closes.

steps: Check that all sub-ledgers, bank and payroll journals are posted
Run the trial balance in AFAS and export to Excel
Compare balances with last month and budget
Investigate odd balances and post corrections
Hand the checked trial balance to the controller
drudgery: Ticking off posted journals by hand
Comparing balances line by line
Chasing missing postings
today.time_sinks: Finding why an account moved and waiting for missing journals from payroll or other teams.

lenses.faster: A close checklist confirms postings automatically and a variance script highlights only accounts outside thresholds.
lenses.autonomous: From day one of the close the trial balance runs daily with variance flags, so problems show up before the deadline.
lenses.ambitious: A soft close every week, which cuts days to close and gives the forecast fresh actuals.
lenses.joy: Line-by-line comparisons go; what remains is investigating real anomalies.
lenses.options: Show variance against last month, last year and budget side by side, so the reviewer picks the relevant lens.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets thresholds and the close checklist and reviews flagged accounts instead of all accounts.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a variance is a real business change or a booking error, and deciding the correction.
tasks.pattern_why: The trial balance is a standard AFAS output; variance checks and completeness checks are fixed rules.

in_practice.trigger: Close calendar day 1, then daily until close.
steps: Script checks that bank, AP, AR, payroll and agency journals are posted
Trial balance pulled from AFAS
Variance rules flag accounts beyond set thresholds
Bookkeeper investigates flags and posts corrections
Controller receives trial balance with flag status
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves corrections; controller signs off the trial balance.
in_practice.logs_to: Close checklist in SharePoint and AFAS journal audit trail.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces trial balances and supports period closing.
Automated variance flagging on trial balances is standard in close tools.

risks: Thresholds set too wide so errors pass
Corrections posted without documentation, hurting the audit trail
Payroll journal timing still blocks the close
research_questions: How many trial balance corrections per month did the auditor or controller find last year?
Which journals arrive late most often, and why?
Can AFAS data be pulled intraday, or only via the nightly extract?

tasks.short: Gather actuals and earlier budgets into the budget templates for the controller and FP&A.

today.trigger: Annual budget round in autumn and quarterly reforecasts.
steps: Export actuals per cost centre from AFAS
Fill department budget templates with last year and year-to-date figures
Send templates to managers and collect returns by email
Merge returned sheets and check totals
Hand the consolidated file to FP&A
drudgery: Prefilling dozens of templates by hand
Chasing managers for returns
Merging sheets with changed layouts
today.time_sinks: Collecting and merging manager returns that come back in different shapes and late.

lenses.faster: Templates are prefilled from AFAS automatically and returns are collected in one structured form, so merging is gone.
lenses.autonomous: Reminders go out to managers who have not returned their sheet, and the consolidation updates as returns come in.
lenses.ambitious: Budgets per site and customer contract, including flex labour by season and CAO wage steps, instead of one line per cost centre.
lenses.joy: No more copying and merging; the bookkeeper talks managers through their numbers instead.
lenses.options: Give each manager a baseline plus two scenarios, for example volume plus or minus 10 percent, to react to.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper designs the data collection and checks, FP&A owns the assumptions.
reach: Payroll Specialist: wage cost projections from CAO steps

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which manager pads their budget, explaining figures to non-finance people, and spotting missing cost items.
tasks.pattern_why: The data work can be automated, but budgets depend on talks with managers and assumptions only people own.

in_practice.trigger: Budget round opens on the finance calendar.
steps: Templates prefilled with actuals and prior budget per cost centre
Managers fill a shared structured form or sheet
Script consolidates returns and flags gaps and big changes
Copilot drafts questions for each manager on outliers
Bookkeeper follows up and hands the clean file to FP&A
in_practice.human_gate: Managers own their numbers; FP&A and the controller approve the consolidated budget.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel can summarise and flag outliers in budget sheets.
Prefilling budget templates from ledger data is a common automation.

risks: Managers anchor on prefilled numbers and stop thinking
Version confusion between returned files
Sensitive salary data in budget sheets shared too widely (AVG)
research_questions: How many budget templates go out each round and how long does merging take today?
Would FP&A rather move to a planning tool than improve the Excel process?
Which managers return late, and what makes them late?

tasks.short: Keep stock records of pallets, packaging, fuel and spare parts in AFAS in line with counts.

today.trigger: Goods receipts, monthly stock counts at the three sites, and month-end valuation.
steps: Book goods receipts and issues from delivery notes and site lists
Collect count sheets from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Compare counts with AFAS stock and book differences
Value stock for the month-end balance
Ask site leads about large differences
drudgery: Typing count sheets into Excel
Chasing sites for missing counts
Booking small differences one by one
today.time_sinks: Waiting for and retyping count sheets from sites, and explaining differences.

lenses.faster: Sites enter counts in a form on a phone, and differences are calculated and proposed as bookings automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Receipts matched to purchase invoices update stock without retyping; small differences under a threshold post automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Accurate monthly stock of pallets and packaging per site, so pallet losses and packaging waste become visible and can be charged to customers.
lenses.joy: No more retyping handwritten count sheets; the work becomes understanding why stock leaks.
lenses.options: Show valuation at last price, average price and standard price so the controller can choose consistently.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets count rules and thresholds and watches difference trends per site.
reach: Controller: stock valuation for the balance sheet
Site operations: pallet balance with customers

tasks.human_edge: Talking to site leads about why counts differ and deciding when a difference is loss, error or theft.
tasks.pattern_why: Stock movements and counts are structured; rules for differences and valuation can be written down, with an optional model to read delivery notes.

in_practice.trigger: Count completed at a site, or a goods receipt is registered.
steps: Site lead enters counts in a Power Apps or Microsoft Forms form
Script compares counts to AFAS stock and calculates differences
Differences under threshold booked; larger ones listed for review
Bookkeeper checks with the site and approves bookings
Month-end valuation runs from approved stock
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves differences above threshold; controller approves valuation method.
data_needed: Item master and stock per site
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS stock mutations with reason codes and a difference log per site.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit has a stock and logistics module for items and stock mutations.
Mobile count forms feeding ERP stock are a common pattern.

risks: Unclear which stock is Noordhaven's own versus customer stock in the WMS
Automatic small-difference bookings hide systematic loss
Site leads see counting as extra work and skip it
research_questions: Which stock items does finance actually keep in AFAS, and what is their value?
How often are counts late or incomplete per site?
Is pallet exchange with customers tracked anywhere today?

tasks.short: Prepare and file BTW returns, ICP and CBS statistics, and support pension and UWV forms.

today.trigger: Monthly or quarterly VAT deadline, CBS requests, and pension fund or UWV requests.
steps: Run the VAT report in AFAS and check the codes per booking
Correct wrongly coded invoices, especially foreign and reverse-charge ones
Fill and submit the BTW and ICP return to the Belastingdienst
Complete CBS statistics and pension fund forms from ledger data
File copies and evidence for the auditor
drudgery: Checking VAT codes on hundreds of invoices
Rekeying figures into government portals
Finding evidence for EU reverse-charge customers
today.time_sinks: Checking VAT codes on cross-border transport and fixing miscoded bookings before the deadline.

lenses.faster: Rules check every booking's VAT code against customer country and VAT number, so the review covers only flagged lines.
lenses.autonomous: A draft BTW and ICP return is ready on day two after period close, with flagged bookings and a reconciliation to the ledger.
lenses.ambitious: VAT codes checked at the moment of booking instead of at the deadline, so returns need almost no correction and supplementation (suppletie) becomes rare.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning invoice lists for wrong VAT codes; the bookkeeper handles the tricky cross-border cases.
lenses.options: Present the draft return with and without disputed items so the controller decides on the treatment.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains VAT rules and the filing calendar and reviews the drafts.

tasks.human_edge: Judging unclear VAT treatment, taking responsibility for filed numbers, and dealing with the Belastingdienst.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across ledger, rules and portals with exceptions; filings carry legal liability, so a person approves before submission.

in_practice.trigger: Filing calendar date after period close.
steps: Pull VAT report and bookings from AFAS
Rules validate VAT codes against country, VAT number (VIES check) and goods or service type
Agent drafts BTW and ICP return and reconciles to the ledger
Bookkeeper resolves flags; controller approves
Return submitted via AFAS or Digipoort and evidence filed
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every return before submission; nothing is filed automatically.
data_needed: Sales and purchase bookings with VAT codes
in_practice.logs_to: Filing register in SharePoint with draft, approval, submission receipt and evidence.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can prepare and send the VAT return electronically to the Belastingdienst.
The EU VIES service validates VAT numbers of EU businesses.

risks: Wrong VAT treatment on cross-border transport leading to assessments and fines
Over-trust in the draft by approvers
Payroll-related filings overlapping with the Payroll Specialist's work
research_questions: How many VAT corrections or suppleties were filed in the last two years, and why?
Which government and pension forms does the bookkeeper actually own versus payroll?
Does AFAS already send the BTW return electronically here, or is it typed into the portal?

role.altitude: From processing invoices, bank lines and reports to running the finance data flow: owning matching rules, VAT and costing rules, close checklists and exception queues, and reporting on touchless rates.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: early dispute and short-payment follow-up
Accountant: balance sheet reconciliations and VAT reconciliation
FP&A Analyst: actuals preparation and budget data collection
role.ceiling_note: Bank matching, reporting and trial balance work could drop by 70-80 percent, but budgets, VAT judgement, stock differences and customer contact stay human; filings and auto-booking rules need controller sign-off and auditor acceptance.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing matching and validation rules in AFAS
Power BI data modelling and data quality checks
Reviewing model output and exception queues critically
Dutch and EU VAT for cross-border transport
role.ambitious_version: The three bookkeepers run a near-touchless procure-to-pay and order-to-cash flow with daily reconciled cash, a weekly soft close and cost prices for every tender, cutting days to close and feeding FP&A a forecast base the business trusts.
